examples.en: That child was admitted to the hospital with malnutrition.
He went hungry for a long time and became malnourished.

examples.ko: 세계 곳곳에서 영양실조 아이들이 도움을 기다려요.
examples.en: Malnourished children around the world are waiting for help.
To prevent malnutrition you need to eat a balanced diet.

examples.ko: 무리한 다이어트가 영양실조를 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: An extreme diet can cause malnutrition.

examples.ko: 의사가 영양실조 증상을 자세히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor explained the symptoms of malnutrition in detail.

explain: 필요한 영양을 충분히 먹지 못해서 몸이 약해진 상태예요. 보통 '영양실조에 걸리다'라고 하고, '영양부족'은 그보다 가벼운 상태에 써요. 병원 이야기나 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I think I'm not getting enough nutrition lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영양실조'보다 가벼운 상태에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a milder condition than 영양실조.

phrases.en: I starved too long and collapsed from malnutrition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심한 상태를 말할 때 원인을 '으로'로 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 로 to give malnutrition as the cause of a severe condition.

phrases.en: Symptoms of malnutrition appeared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in hospitals and news.

explain_en: Illness from not getting enough food or nutrients. A condition in which the body is weak because it does not get enough nutrients. It is usually 영양실조에 걸리다, and 영양부족 is used for a milder state. You hear it in hospital talk and the news.

examples.en: After long treatment, the illness was completely cured.

examples.ko: 이 병은 일찍 발견하면 완치될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If this disease is found early, it can be completely cured.
To be fully cured, you have to keep taking the medicine.
Grandmother was fully cured and left the hospital.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 곧 나을 거라고 하시고 완치된 환자도 많다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said I will get better soon and that many patients were fully cured.
You need to rest from exercise until you are fully cured.

explain: '낫다'는 감기 같은 가벼운 병에도 쓰지만 '완치되다'는 오래 치료한 병에 주로 써요. '완치율', '완치 판정'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I got a doctor's confirmation of full recovery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 병이 다 나았다고 확인받을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a hospital confirms the illness is completely cured.

phrases.en: This illness is hard to cure completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 어렵다'를 붙여 완전히 낫기 힘든 병을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -기 어렵다 it describes illnesses that are hard to cure fully.

phrases.example: 병이 완치돼서 이제 일할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: My illness is fully cured, so I can work now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'로 이어 완치된 뒤의 이유나 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어서 it connects being cured to its result or reason.

explain_en: Passive form, illness is cured completely, subject is the patient or disease. 낫다 works for light illnesses like a cold, but 완치되다 is mostly for illnesses treated for a long time. It also appears often in nouns like 완치율 (cure rate) and 완치 판정 (declared cured).

examples.en: I got a stomach ulcer because of stress.

examples.ko: 위궤양이 있으면 매운 음식을 피하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If you have a stomach ulcer, it's best to avoid spicy food.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 위궤양 약을 처방해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor prescribed me medicine for a stomach ulcer.
I heard a stomach ulcer can heal with treatment.
My father was hospitalized last month because of a stomach ulcer.

examples.ko: 속이 계속 쓰려서 위궤양인지 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: My stomach kept burning, so I got tested to see if it was an ulcer.

explain: '위염'은 위 안쪽에 염증이 생긴 것이고, '위궤양'은 위 안쪽 점막이 패여 상처가 난 상태라서 서로 달라요. '위궤양에 걸리다', '위궤양 진단을 받다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Stomach ulcer symptoms are heartburn and stomach pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병의 증세를 설명할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used to explain the signs of the illness.

phrases.en: I'm getting treatment for a stomach ulcer at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에 다니며 치료하는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes going to a hospital for treatment.
phrases.en_equiv: to receive treatment for a stomach ulcer

phrases.en: My stomach ulcer healed after I took the medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 좋아졌을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the illness has gotten better.

explain_en: '위염' is inflammation of the stomach lining, while '위궤양' is when the lining is eroded into a sore, so they are different. It is used as '위궤양에 걸리다' or '위궤양 진단을 받다'.

en: to be in a critical condition

examples.en: Grandfather's condition is critical, so the family gathered.
I heard the patient's condition is very critical.

examples.ko: 위중한 상황이지만 의료진이 최선을 다하고 있어요.
examples.en: It is a critical situation, but the medical staff are doing their best.
The person who was in the accident is in critical condition.

examples.ko: 병원에서 상태가 위중하니 빨리 오라고 했어요.
examples.en: The hospital said his condition is critical and told me to come quickly.
My father is critically ill, so I took leave from work.

explain: 주로 병세나 환자의 상태가 생명이 걱정될 만큼 나쁠 때 써요. '위독하다'와 비슷하고, 윗사람 이야기를 할 때는 '위중하세요/위중하셔서'처럼 높여요.

phrases.example: 환자가 위중한 상태라서 면회가 안 돼요.
phrases.en: The patient is in critical condition, so visits aren't allowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 이야기에서 '상태'를 꾸밀 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form when modifying '상태' in hospital talk.

phrases.en: My grandmother is in a very serious condition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람의 병세를 말할 때 높여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for talking about an elder's condition.

phrases.en: I got word that my father is critically ill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같지만, '위독하다'는 생명이 위험하다는 느낌이 더 직접적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, but '위독하다' sounds more directly life-threatening.

explain_en: Formal, an illness or condition that is life-threatening (병이 위중하다) It is mainly used when an illness or a patient's condition is bad enough that life is at risk. It is close to '위독하다', and for someone senior you raise it as '위중하세요' or '위중하셔서'.

examples.ko: 시끄러운 곳에 다녀온 뒤 이명이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After visiting a noisy place, I got ringing in my ears.

examples.ko: 밤에 조용하면 이명이 더 크게 들려요.
examples.en: When it is quiet at night, the ringing sounds louder.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님께 이명 때문에 왔다고 말했어요.
examples.en: I told the doctor I came because of tinnitus.

examples.ko: 이명 증상이 심해서 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: My tinnitus is bad, so I can't sleep well.
Tinnitus gets worse when I am tired.
My father has had tinnitus for a long time.

explain: 의학 용어라 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 친구끼리는 '귀에서 삐 소리가 나요'처럼 풀어서 말할 때가 많아요. '이명이 있다', '이명이 들리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I have tinnitus in my right ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이명이 계속 있는 상태를 말하는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to say one has ongoing tinnitus.

phrases.example: 이명 증상이 심하면 병원에 가 보세요.
phrases.en: If your tinnitus symptoms are severe, go see a doctor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증상'과 함께 써서 병원이나 건강 정보에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 증상; common in clinics and health information.

phrases.en: When I'm tired, my tinnitus gets worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이명이 더 크거나 자주 들리게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when tinnitus becomes louder or more frequent.

explain_en: It is a medical term, so it mainly appears at the hospital or in health talk. Among friends people often say it in plain words, like 'there is a beeping sound in my ear'. It goes with 이명이 있다 and 이명이 들리다.

examples.ko: 땀을 많이 흘렸으면 전해질을 보충해야 해요.
examples.en: If you've sweated a lot, you need to replenish electrolytes.

examples.ko: 이 이온 음료에는 전해질이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This sports drink contains electrolytes.

examples.ko: 몸속 전해질 균형이 깨지면 어지러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the electrolyte balance in your body is upset, you can feel dizzy.

examples.ko: 운동 후에 전해질 음료를 마시는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people drink electrolyte drinks after exercising.

examples.ko: 토하고 나면 수분뿐 아니라 전해질도 잃어요.
examples.en: After vomiting, you lose not only water but also electrolytes.
There is a substance called an electrolyte inside a battery.

explain: 몸에서는 나트륨, 칼륨처럼 물에 녹아 몸의 균형을 맞추는 성분을 말해요. 보통 '전해질 음료', '전해질 보충', '전해질 불균형'처럼 쓰고, 배터리 이야기에서도 나와요. '전해지다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 운동한 뒤에는 전해질 음료를 한 병 마셔요.
phrases.en: After working out, I drink a bottle of an electrolyte drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 땀으로 빠진 성분을 채워 주는 음료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing and refers to a drink that replaces what is lost through sweat.

phrases.example: 더운 날에는 물과 함께 전해질 보충도 해야 해요.
phrases.en: On hot days, you need to replenish electrolytes as well as drink water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보충'과 함께 써서 부족한 전해질을 채운다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 보충, it means making up for a shortage of electrolytes.

phrases.example: 심하게 토하면 전해질 불균형이 생길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you vomit a lot, you can end up with an electrolyte imbalance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의학 이야기에서 몸의 전해질 양이 맞지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In medical talk, this describes the amounts of electrolytes in the body being out of balance.

explain_en: In the body, it refers to substances like sodium and potassium that dissolve in water and keep the body balanced. It is usually used in phrases like '전해질 음료', '전해질 보충', and '전해질 불균형', and also appears in talk about batteries. It is completely different from the verb '전해지다'.

en: to cut; to cut open; to incise

examples.en: The doctor made an incision in the abdomen and operated.
To operate, you first have to cut the skin open.
They wrapped a bandage over the incision.
They cut through the mountain and made a new road.
Surgery with a small incision heals faster.
They opened the wound and cleaned inside.

explain: '자르다'와 달리 '절개하다'는 수술을 위해 몸을 열거나 공사를 위해 산을 가를 때처럼 필요한 부분만 정확히 가르는 느낌이에요. 병원과 공사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The incision area still hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수술로 갈라 연 곳을 말할 때 병원에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in hospitals for the spot opened in surgery.

phrases.en: The doctor cut open the wound and drained the pus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈라서 연 다음에 이어지는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links what was done after cutting something open.

phrases.example: 배를 절개하지 않고 수술하는 방법도 있어요.
phrases.en: There is also a way to operate without cutting the belly open.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않고'로 갈라서 열지 않는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -지 않고, describes a method that avoids cutting open.

explain_en: Cut open with a blade — surgery (배를 절개하다) Unlike '자르다' (to cut), '절개하다' feels like cutting open only the necessary part precisely, such as opening the body for surgery or cutting through a mountain for construction. It often appears in talk about hospitals and construction.

t90.ax: They wrapped a bandage over the incision.

examples.ko: 이 병원에는 중환자가 많아서 늘 바빠요.
examples.en: This hospital has many critical patients, so it's always busy.
The doctor examined the critical patient first.
Visits to critical patients are restricted.
Even family members can't enter the intensive care unit freely.
The nurse is giving medicine to the critical patient.

examples.ko: 중환자 이송 때문에 길이 잠깐 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked for a moment because of a critical patient's transfer.

explain: '중환자실'이라는 말로 병원 이야기나 드라마에서 자주 들려요. 환자를 높여 말할 때는 보통 '환자분'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My grandfather is in the intensive care unit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word in hospital-related talk.

phrases.en: The nurse takes care of critical patients all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 아픈 사람을 보살필 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for caring for seriously ill people at a hospital.

phrases.en: The number of critical patients goes up in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 환자 수의 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news to describe changes in patient numbers.

explain_en: You often hear it in the word '중환자실' (intensive care unit) in hospital talk and dramas. To refer to a patient politely, people usually say '환자분'.

examples.en: My shoulders hurt, so I went to get acupressure.

examples.ko: 지압 매트 위에 서면 발바닥이 시원해요.
examples.en: Standing on an acupressure mat makes the soles of my feet feel refreshed.
They say pressing on the palm helps with headaches.

examples.ko: 이 지압 도구는 목에 쓰기 좋아요.
examples.en: This acupressure tool is good for using on the neck.
Mom helped my digestion with acupressure.

examples.ko: 지압 슬리퍼를 신고 걸으니 발이 너무 아파요.
examples.en: Walking in acupressure slippers really hurts my feet.

explain: '마사지'는 문지르고 주무르는 것이고, '지압'은 손가락이나 도구로 몸의 한 곳을 꾹 누르는 것이에요. '지압을 받다', '지압 매트', '지압 슬리퍼'처럼 많이 써요. 아프지만 시원한 느낌이 있어서 발바닥, 어깨, 목에 자주 해요.

phrases.example: 지압 슬리퍼를 신고 집 안을 걸어 다녀요.
phrases.en: I walk around the house wearing acupressure slippers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥이 울퉁불퉁해서 발바닥을 눌러 주는 슬리퍼예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slippers with a bumpy sole that press on the soles of your feet.

phrases.en: After an acupressure massage, my body feels lighter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누르는 방식의 마사지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a massage that works by pressing on points.

phrases.en: When I'm tired, I do acupressure on my palm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 몸을 눌러 풀어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when pressing on your own body to relieve tension.

explain_en: '마사지' means rubbing and kneading, while '지압' means pressing firmly on one spot with fingers or a tool. You often hear '지압을 받다', '지압 매트' and '지압 슬리퍼'. It hurts a bit but feels good, and is often done on the soles of the feet, shoulders and neck.

en: to spread rampantly; to break out

examples.en: An epidemic is raging in that region.

examples.ko: 여름이 되면 모기가 창궐해서 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: In summer, mosquitoes swarm and I cannot sleep.

examples.ko: 과거에는 콜레라가 창궐했고 많은 사람이 고통받았어요.
examples.en: In the past cholera ran rampant and many people suffered.
We disinfect regularly so that pests do not run rampant.

examples.ko: 바이러스가 창궐하던 시기에 마스크를 늘 썼어요.
examples.en: During the time the virus was spreading wildly, I always wore a mask.

examples.ko: 가짜 뉴스가 창궐하는 요즘, 출처를 꼭 확인해요.
examples.en: These days, when fake news is rampant, I always check the source.

explain: 전염병, 해충, 나쁜 소문처럼 안 좋은 것이 걷잡을 수 없이 퍼질 때 써요. 좋은 것이 널리 퍼질 때는 쓰지 않아요. '유행하다'보다 훨씬 부정적인 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Pests ran rampant on the farm and spoiled the crops.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레가 한꺼번에 크게 늘어날 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for insects suddenly multiplying in large numbers.

phrases.en: The bad rumor spread widely and fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말이고 '창궐하다'만큼 걷잡을 수 없는 느낌은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word, without the same out-of-control feeling.

phrases.example: 창궐하는 바이러스를 막으려고 모두 마스크를 썼어요.
phrases.en: Everyone wore masks to stop the rampant virus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '창궐하는'을 명사 앞에 붙여 퍼지는 것을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '창궐하는' placed before a noun describes what is spreading.

explain_en: It is used when something bad, such as disease, pests or rumors, spreads out of control. It is not used for good things spreading. It feels much more negative than '유행하다'.

examples.ko: 코가 막히고 머리가 아파서 병원에 갔더니 축농증이래요.
examples.en: My nose was blocked and my head hurt, so I went to the hospital, and they said it's sinusitis.

examples.ko: 축농증 때문에 냄새를 잘 못 맡아요.
examples.en: I can't smell well because of my sinusitis.
Sinusitis is similar to a cold, but it lasts longer.
I have suffered from sinusitis since I was little.
My sinusitis got worse, so I had surgery.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 축농증에는 코 세척이 도움이 된다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said nasal rinsing helps with sinusitis.

explain: 병원에서는 '부비동염'이라고도 하지만 일상 대화에서는 '축농증'이라는 말을 훨씬 많이 써요. 보통 '축농증에 걸리다', '축농증이 있다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: My cold dragged on and turned into a sinus infection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 생겼다는 사실을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for saying you came down with the condition.

phrases.en: I've had sinusitis since I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래된 증상이나 지병처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a long-standing condition.

phrases.example: 코가 너무 불편해서 축농증 수술을 받았어요.
phrases.en: My nose bothered me so much that I had sinus surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료나 병원 이야기에서 다른 명사와 붙여서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often combined with other nouns in talk about treatment and hospitals.

explain_en: Doctors may also say '부비동염', but in everyday talk '축농증' is used much more. People usually say '축농증에 걸리다' or '축농증이 있다'.

examples.en: Eating even your friend's share is really petty.

examples.ko: 그런 치사한 방법으로 이기고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to win by such a low-down method.
Don't be petty and get angry over something like this.
It's a bit petty, but I went first and saved a seat.
It's so petty that I don't even want to talk about it anymore.
Even if you think it's petty, I can't help it.

explain: '치사하다'는 친구 사이에서 서운할 때 투덜대듯 쓰는 구어체 표현이에요. 작은 이익을 따지거나 비겁하게 굴 때 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 무례하게 들려요. '인색하다'는 돈을 아끼는 것에만 써서 쓰임이 더 좁아요.

phrases.en: I was upset because my friend was acting petty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게 굴다'로 치사한 행동을 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-게 굴다' describes someone acting in a petty way.

phrases.en: Please don't do such a petty thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비겁하거나 얄미운 행동을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a mean or sneaky act.

phrases.en: This is so petty that I'm not doing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치사해서'는 일이 못마땅해서 그만두겠다고 투덜댈 때 쓰는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual complaint used when you refuse something because it feels petty.

explain_en: 치사하다 is a colloquial word you grumble to friends when you feel let down. It is for someone fussing over small gains or acting underhand. Said to an elder it sounds rude. 인색하다 only covers being stingy with money, so it is narrower.

examples.ko: 콩팥은 몸속의 나쁜 물질을 걸러 내요.
examples.en: The kidneys filter out bad substances in the body.

examples.ko: 아버지가 콩팥이 안 좋아서 병원에 다니세요.
examples.en: My father has weak kidneys and goes to the hospital.

examples.ko: 짠 음식을 너무 많이 먹으면 콩팥에 부담이 가요.
examples.en: Eating too much salty food puts a strain on your kidneys.

examples.ko: 콩팥 두 개 중 하나만 있어도 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can live with just one of your two kidneys.
I read the story of a person who donated a kidney.
You need to take care of your kidneys, too.

explain: 한자어 '신장'도 같은 장기를 가리켜요. 병원에서는 '신장 기능'처럼 한자어를 더 자주 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 순우리말 콩팥을 많이 써요. 몸 설명에서는 '간', '폐'처럼 장기 이름과 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: The hospital tested my kidney function.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콩팥과 같은 장기이고 병원에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same organ, used more often in hospitals.

phrases.en: I heard the kidney function has improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콩팥이 일을 잘하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how well the kidneys work.

phrases.en: I'm getting a kidney test tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 검사를 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting tested at a hospital.

explain_en: The Sino-Korean word 신장 also names the same organ. Hospitals more often use 신장, as in 신장 기능, while everyday talk uses the native Korean 콩팥. In body explanations it appears alongside organs like 간 and 폐.

examples.ko: 탈수가 끝나면 빨래를 바로 꺼내 널어요.
examples.en: When the spin cycle ends, I take the laundry out and hang it right away.

examples.ko: 탈수 시간을 너무 길게 하면 옷이 구겨져요.
examples.en: If you make the spin time too long, the clothes get wrinkled.
The washing machine shakes a lot during the spin cycle.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 탈수까지 하면 모양이 변해요.
examples.en: If you spin this garment too, it loses its shape.

examples.ko: 땀을 많이 흘려서 탈수 증상이 왔어요.
examples.en: I sweated a lot and got symptoms of dehydration.

examples.ko: 탈수만 따로 한 번 더 돌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please run just the spin cycle one more time.

explain: 세탁기의 '세탁, 헹굼, 탈수' 중 물기를 짜내는 단계를 말해요. 열로 말리는 '건조'와는 달라요. 몸에 물이 부족해지는 '탈수 증상'에도 같은 말을 써요.

phrases.example: 더운 날 물을 안 마시면 탈수 증상이 생겨요.
phrases.en: If you don't drink water on a hot day, you get symptoms of dehydration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세탁기가 아니라 몸에 물이 부족할 때 쓰는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the body meaning, not the washing machine one.

phrases.en: When the rinse is done, I press the spin-dry button.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세탁기를 직접 다루는 장면에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used when operating a washing machine.

phrases.en: My washing machine won't spin-dry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세탁기가 제대로 작동하지 않을 때 쓰는 문제 상황 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a problem when the machine isn't working properly.

explain_en: It is the stage in a washing machine's 'wash, rinse, spin' cycle where water is wrung out. It differs from '건조', which dries with heat. The same word is also used for the body lacking water, as in '탈수 증상' (dehydration symptoms).

examples.en: The medication times are morning and evening.

examples.ko: 간호사가 투약 전에 이름을 다시 확인했어요.
examples.en: The nurse rechecked my name before giving the medication.
Wrong medication can be dangerous.
It has been a week since the medication started.

examples.ko: 아이의 투약 기록을 수첩에 적고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm writing my child's medication record in a notebook.

examples.ko: 약국에서 투약 방법을 자세히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The pharmacy explained in detail how to take the medicine.

explain: 병원과 약국에서 쓰는 전문적인 말이에요. 일상에서는 '약을 먹다', '약을 먹이다'라고 해요. '투약 시간', '투약 기록', '투약량'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: The doctor reduced the dosage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번에 또는 하루에 주는 약의 양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to the amount of medicine given at once or per day.

phrases.en: The nurse writes the medication record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 언제 어떤 약을 줬는지 적은 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the hospital record of which medicine was given and when.

phrases.example: 지금 투약 중이라 술을 마시면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: I'm on medication now, so I can't drink alcohol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약을 계속 먹거나 맞는 동안을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the period when someone is continuing to take medicine.

explain_en: This is a technical word used in hospitals and pharmacies. In daily life, people say '약을 먹다' (take medicine) or '약을 먹이다' (give medicine to someone). It often has another word after it, as in '투약 시간', '투약 기록', and '투약량'.
